prompt: A clear cutaway illustration of a modern grocery shop operating as a connected system: at the front, customers use self-checkout kiosks and a vending-style pickup locker, with one shopper scanning an item successfully while another faces a payment-error screen and presses a prominent “help” button; a nearby human employee assists them, showing that automation does not eliminate staff. Across the aisles, a shelf-stocking robot pauses beside a spilled item, an accessible checkout is usable by a wheelchair user, and electronic shelf labels link by visible data lines to an inventory dashboard. In the background, a warehouse conveyor sorts boxes while a worker restocks a machine, and small visual callouts show practical disruptions—an out-of-stock shelf, a security alert, a jammed scanner, and a robot needing charging—contrasted with smooth flows of goods and data, conveying that retail automation succeeds through reliable operation, maintenance, safety, and human support rather than a single impressive machine.
